pool.text: There was an important armed engagement involving the city of Lille in this year.
The first written mention of the town of Lille appeared under a Latin name.
Saint-Sauveur parish was established, later naming a modern-day district in the city.
The Countess's Hospital was founded by Jeanne in the city of Lille.
Antoine Tack became the very first printer to set up shop in Lille.
Lille officially became French under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle after a successful siege.
Albert Calmette and Camille Guérin discovered the first anti-tuberculosis vaccine at the Pasteur Institute.
Roger Salengro became Minister of the Interior before facing a tragic campaign against him.
British, Canadian and Polish troops liberated the départements of Nord and Pas-de-Calais.
The world's first automated rapid transit underground network opened in Lille.
Construction began on the brand-new Euralille business district to improve accessibility.
A high-speed TGV train line opened to connect Paris with Lille.
The Grand Palais opened for the general public in Lille.
Lille was selected and celebrated as a European Capital of Culture alongside Genoa.
Urban centers including Lille and Roubaix were affected by civil riots.
The city of Lille was officially awarded the label Internet City.
The Eurometropolis Lille-Kortrijk-Tournai was created as the first European grouping of territorial cooperation.
The city of Lille and suburban municipalities formed the European Metropolis of Lille.
The European metropolis of Lille was awarded the title World Design Capital.
The Saint-Joseph Chapel of Saint-Paul College was demolished.
